However, you hit on something that a lot of people seem to not understand about 1984.

The main control they used in 1984 was not surveillance. That might be the most obvious one in the book, but there were so many other methods of control and suppression. The biggest one was control of language. It was no longer possible for people to protest because the government had simply removed the words. People could not express their feelings because they did not have the language to do it. The next most powerful one was they literally changed their own history when they needed to. They revised every publicly available item to reflect what the current truth and history was. The mass surveillance, while being the most overt method of control, was really also the weakest. It was there for the appearance of control. The government had other methods of actual control.

So, while having a shitload of surveillance is a problem and should be addressed, we are nowhere close to the world described in 1984.

1984 was written just post World War II and the entire thing was a warning about the future of totalitarian regimes. All the things he wrote about as futuristic sci fi elements were just extreme versions of things he observed in real life happening in Nazi Germany and Russia. These were things like the state controlling the media to promote the states propoganda, creating a fear culture where people are attacked for expressing certain words or ideas, and of course the massive intrusion and spying by audio and video recording.
